name: AWS EC2 Spot Instances (interruptible GPU capacity, general)
price_basis: NO price_usd recorded, deliberately. AWS advertises a discount of 'up to 90% off compared to On-Demand' and states prices 'adjust gradually based on long-term trends in supply and demand', but the concrete per-SKU spot table renders client-side from describe-spot-price-history and spot-price.s3.amazonaws.com/spotprice.js returned HTTP 403 when fetched 2026-10-03. A derived or remembered spot rate would be invented.
notes: A structural record rather than a price record. Spot is the cheapest credible route to AWS Hopper and Blackwell capacity by a wide margin when it works - independent neocloud evidence elsewhere in this slice puts H100 spot at roughly 40% of the on-demand rate - and it is the real answer to the p5 allocation problem. The catch is interruption: AWS reclaims Spot instances on a two-minute warning, and the p5 SKUs are exactly those with the deepest demand pools and therefore the worst interruption profile. Practical guidance: Spot for fault-tolerant training with checkpoint resume, never for an interactive inference endpoint; Capacity Blocks when the pool must still be there tomorrow. 'Up to 90% off' is a ceiling across all EC2 SKUs, not the H100 discount specifically. Note the same mutual-exclusion logic as on Google Cloud, where the pricing page states explicitly that Spot VMs and preemptible VMs cannot receive CUDs or SUDs: never model a Spot instance as if it were also earning a commitment discount.
